title: The Paleobiology Database application programming interface
authors: Peters, S.E.; McClennen, M.

title: Denormalized occurrence and taxon tables of the Paleobiology Database
authors: The Paleobiology Database Community; Kocsis, Á.T.
datasetSnapshot: PBDB full taxon table downloaded 2026-07-19; pbdb_taxa_csv.zip MD5 fca5fde5e8d5922d06fe332a42b955f9

title: Open Tree of Life web services
authors: OpenTreeOfLife Project
note: Topology and taxonomy context; divergence dates require separate evidence.

title: The Late Precambrian fossil Kimberella is a mollusc-like bilaterian organism
authors: Fedonkin, M.A.; Waggoner, B.M.
note: More than 35 White Sea specimens document a bilaterally symmetrical benthic organism with a non-mineralized dorsal cover; molluscan affinity is an interpretation rather than an observed crown assignment.

title: A soft-bodied mollusc with radula from the Middle Cambrian Burgess Shale
authors: Caron, J.-B.; Scheltema, A.; Schander, C.; Rudkin, D.
note: A 189-specimen Burgess Shale sample documents a serially replaced feeding apparatus interpreted as a molluscan radula together with a broad foot and mantle-groove structures.

title: Halwaxiids and the early evolution of the lophotrochozoans
authors: Conway Morris, S.; Caron, J.-B.
note: Orthrozanclus combines an anterior shell, Wiwaxia-like sclerites and long spines; the proposed Halwaxiida and its lophotrochozoan position are morphology-matrix hypotheses.

title: Shell microstructure of the early bivalve Pojetaia and the independent origin of nacre within the Mollusca
authors: Vendrasco, M.J.; Checa, A.G.; Kouchinsky, A.V.
note: New Pojetaia and Fordilla shell sections document laminar inner fabrics interpreted as foliated aragonite rather than undisputed Cambrian nacre.

title: Primitive soft-bodied cephalopods from the Cambrian
authors: Smith, M.R.; Caron, J.-B.
note: Ninety newly prepared Burgess Shale specimens reveal paired camera-like eyes, a funnel, lateral fins and two tentacles; cephalopod affinity remains debated because diagnostic hard-part and mouthpart evidence is absent.

title: Phylogenomics reveals deep molluscan relationships
authors: Kocot, K.M.; Cannon, J.T.; Todt, C.; Citarella, M.R.; Kohn, A.B.; Meyer, A.; Santos, S.R.; Schander, C.; Moroz, L.L.; Lieb, B.; Halanych, K.M.
note: Transcriptome and genome data from all major molluscan lineages except Monoplacophora support sampled Aculifera and a gastropod–bivalve clade under the reported models.

title: Resolving the evolutionary relationships of molluscs with phylogenomic tools
authors: Smith, S.A.; Wilson, N.G.; Goetz, F.E.; Feehery, C.; Andrade, S.C.S.; Rouse, G.W.; Giribet, G.; Dunn, C.W.
note: New transcriptomes for 15 species bring every major living molluscan group, including Monoplacophora, into sampled matrices; several deep conchiferan nodes differ from other studies.

title: Nodal signalling is involved in left–right asymmetry in snails
authors: Grande, C.; Patel, N.H.
note: Lottia and Biomphalaria embryos show opposite-sided nodal and Pitx expression, and pharmacological inhibition links the pathway to shell chirality in the sampled gastropods.

title: The octopus genome and the evolution of cephalopod neural and morphological novelties
authors: Albertin, C.B.; Simakov, O.; Mitros, T.; Wang, Z.Y.; Pungor, J.R.; Edsinger-Gonzales, E.; Brenner, S.; Ragsdale, C.W.; Rokhsar, D.S.
note: A male Octopus bimaculoides genome plus twelve tissue transcriptomes test gene-family expansion and genome rearrangement without supporting a cephalopod whole-genome duplication.

title: The Early Cambrian tommotiid Micrina, a sessile bivalved stem group brachiopod
authors: Holmer, L.E.; Skovsted, C.B.; Brock, G.A.; Valentine, J.L.; Paterson, J.R.
note: Mitral and sellate sclerites were physically reconstructed as a sessile bivalved organism; homology with brachiopod valves is an explicit stem-group hypothesis.

title: Rhynchonelliformean brachiopods with soft-tissue preservation from the Early Cambrian Chengjiang Lagerstätte of South China
authors: Zhang, Z.; Shu, D.; Emig, C.; Zhang, X.; Han, J.; Liu, J.; Li, Y.; Guo, J.
note: Kutorgina chengjiangensis specimens preserve valves, an early spirolophe-stage lophophore, digestive tract and pedicle in the Chengjiang Lagerstätte.

title: The Lingula genome provides insights into brachiopod evolution and the origin of phosphate biomineralization
authors: Luo, Y.-J.; Takeuchi, T.; Koyanagi, R.; Yamada, L.; Kanda, M.; Khalturina, M.; Fujie, M.; Yamasaki, S.; Endo, K.; Satoh, N. et al.
note: A 425-Mb Lingula anatina genome, developmental and adult transcriptomes, and shell proteome test lophotrochozoan relationships and lineage-specific phosphate biomineralization.

title: An early Cambrian agglutinated tubular lophophorate with brachiopod characters
authors: Zhang, Z.F.; Li, G.X.; Holmer, L.E.; Brock, G.A.; Balthasar, U.; Skovsted, C.B.; Fu, D.J.; Zhang, X.L.; Wang, H.Z.; Butler, A. et al.
note: Yuganotheca elegans combines paired agglutinated valves, a horseshoe-shaped lophophore, a bipartite tube and a long pedicle; its exact position relative to phoronids and brachiopods remains interpretive.

title: A new graptolite (Pterobranchia) from the early Cambrian Xiaoshiba Lagerstätte of China
authors: Yang, J.; Caron, J.-B.; Conway Morris, S.; et al.
note: Five specimens of Yunotubus from the Stage 3 Hongjingshao Formation preserve tubes and colonial soft anatomy; morphology matrices test rather than assume pterobranch affinity.

title: A supra-ordinal classification of the Brachiopoda
authors: Williams, A.; Carlson, S.J.; Brunton, C.H.C.; Holmer, L.E.; Popov, L.
publisher: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
note: Revision replacing the traditional Articulata–Inarticulata split with phylogenetically informed higher groups; Articulata is retained only as a historical navigation grade.

title: A revised classification of the spiriferid brachiopods
authors: Carter, J.L.; Johnson, J.G.; Gourvennec, R.; Hou, H.-F.
note: Order-level systematic revision based on shell characters; classification does not set a global origin, extinction, or direct ancestor.

title: Testing Species Assignments in Extant Terebratulide Brachiopods: A Three-dimensional Geometric Morphometric Analysis of Long-Looped Brachidia
authors: López Carranza, N.; Carlson, S.J.
note: Three-dimensional morphometric test of selected living long-looped terebratulides; it does not characterize every Terebratulida lineage.

title: A new cladistic insight on comparative anatomy and phylogeny of rudists (Bivalvia, Hippuritida)
authors: Rineau, V.; Masse, J.-P.; Villier, L.
note: Forty-one shell characters test sampled rudist relationships; topology is not a global fossil-range endpoint.

title: Phylogenetic analysis of the subclass Pteriomorphia (Bivalvia) from mtDNA COI sequences
authors: Matsumoto, M.
note: Single-locus mitochondrial analysis of sampled pteriomorph bivalves including oysters; rank and topology are study-specific.

title: Phylogenomic analyses of deep gastropod relationships reject Orthogastropoda
authors: Zapata, F.; Wilson, N.G.; Howison, M.; et al.
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Phylogenomic matrices of sampled gastropods reject Orthogastropoda; remaining deep nodes depend on matrices and models.

title: A multi-gene phylogeny of Cephalopoda supports convergent morphological evolution in association with multiple habitat shifts in the marine environment
authors: Lindgren, A.R.; Pankey, M.S.; Hochberg, F.G.; Oakley, T.H.
note: Multigene topology and mapped habitats for sampled living cephalopods; fossil lineages and ancestral ecology remain outside direct sampling.

title: Allonautilus: a new genus of living nautiloid cephalopod and its bearing on phylogeny of the Nautilida
authors: Ward, P.D.; Saunders, W.B.
note: Living Allonautilus anatomy compared with Nautilus and selected fossils; Nautilida evidence cannot bound the broader historical Nautiloidea route.

title: Ammonoids across the Permian/Triassic boundary: a cladistic perspective
authors: McGowan, A.J.; Smith, A.B.
note: Cladistic analysis of sampled boundary-crossing ammonoids; it addresses survival and turnover near one interval, not the full Ammonoidea range.

title: The Lazarus ammonoid family Goniatitidae, the tetrangularly coiled Entogonitidae, and Mississippian biogeography
authors: Korn, D.; Klug, C.; Mapes, R.H.
note: Family-level Mississippian material and biogeographic synthesis within Goniatitida; it cannot define the whole order's endpoints.

title: Origin of the Ceratitida (Ammonoidea) inferred from the early internal shell features
authors: Shigeta, Y.; Zakharov, Y.D.; Mapes, R.H.
note: Comparative internal-shell analysis infers ceratitid relationships; inferred origin is not an observed ancestor or a complete global record.

title: The phylogeny of Hildoceratidae (Cephalopoda, Ammonitida) resolved by an integrated coding scheme of the conch
authors: Bardin, J.; Rouget, I.; Cecca, F.
note: Integrated conch-character matrix for one ammonitid family; its topology is a local test rather than the order's complete history.

title: Molecular clocks indicate turnover and diversification of modern coleoid cephalopods during the Mesozoic Marine Revolution
authors: Tanner, A.R.; Fuchs, D.; Winkelmann, I.E.; et al.
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Fossil-calibrated molecular clocks for sampled modern coleoids; posterior ages are model estimates, not fossil first appearances.

title: Bayesian inference reveals a complex evolutionary history of belemnites
authors: Stevens, K.; Pohle, A.; Hoffmann, R.; Immenhauser, A.
note: Tip-dated morphological analysis of sampled belemnites; topology and node ages remain model- and character-dependent.

title: A mitogenomic phylogeny of chitons (Mollusca: Polyplacophora)
authors: Irisarri, I.; Uribe, J.E.; Eernisse, D.J.; Zardoya, R.
note: Mitogenomic topology from newly sequenced and public chitons; mitochondrial sampling and fossil-calibration ambiguity bound deep inference.

title: Phylogenomics of Aplacophora (Mollusca, Aculifera) and a solenogaster without a foot
authors: Kocot, K.M.; Todt, C.; Mikkelsen, N.T.; Halanych, K.M.
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Phylogenomic analysis of sampled solenogasters and caudofoveates; the legacy Aplacophora label is retained as a historical navigation grade, not assumed to be an exact natural group.
